title: Pilot polyphase TTFT + kernel sync
topics: TTFT (time to first token) regression observed
sequence length skew and kernel selection
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on TTFT regressions after recent kernel update. Auburn observed spikes during 1-2% of requests - correlated to long seqlens and streaming handshake. Redwood SE suggested polyphase hedging (fast narrow kernel + fallback), KV/prefix cache tuning and slight batching changes. Action items: run microbench with prioritized seqlen distribution, share perf spreadsheet and security docs, schedule 2-hour lab to run kernel A/B on customer workload.
next_steps: Redwood to share updated perf spreadsheet + config diffs (Priya) by 2027-11-19
Aurelia to provide 1 hour of request logs and 500 sample prompts (anonymized) by 2027-11-19
Schedule 2-hour lab for kernel A/B test week of 2027-11-22 (Jordan to send Doodle)
Priya to push small runtime change to reduce early handshake for streaming by 2027-11-20
action_items: Priya Rao - produce perf spreadsheet and config diffs - due 2027-11-19
Aurelia (Sasha) - supply 500 anonymized prompts + logs - due 2027-11-19
Jordan Kim - send Doodle for 2-hour lab windows - due 2027-11-18

transcript:
Header: 2027-11-17 15:00 UTC | Duration ~50m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Luca Moretti (Redwood CSM); Sasha Patel (Aurelia lead), Miguel Rivera (Aurelia platform), Tanya Li (Aurelia SRE), Robert Chen (Aurelia PM)
Shared artifacts: perf spreadsheet link: https://redwood.app/sheets/polyphase-2027-11, security deck: https://redwood.app/docs/sec-redwood-enterprise.pdf

[00:00] Jordan: okay everyone thanks for joining, we have about 50 minutes. quick rundown — priya's gonna walk through the kernel telemetry then we'll go into the microburst traces you sent, sasha, and then agree next steps. any urgent items before we start?
[00:12] Sasha: no, just the TTFT spikes — those are the ones we want to squeeze down. we've seen 1 to 1.5 second tail outliers, not consistent but enough to break our UI budget.
[00:23] Priya: yup, and we dug in this week. initial hypothesis is interplay between streaming handshake + long sequence length requests causing kernel selection to pick the "wider matrix kernel" which has higher latency on first token. there may also be a small kv cache miss pattern.
[00:40] Miguel: when you say "wider matrix kernel" do you mean the fused attention kernel or the generic matmul path? sometimes the model picks the fallback matmul on certain seqlens.
[00:51] Priya: good call — i mean the wider fused path; the runtime heuristics pick it when seqlen > 1024 for this model variant. but on streaming + small generated tokens it costs us on TTFT.
[01:05] Robert: is this a change after the recent kernel update? we rolled the update three days ago.
[01:10] Priya: yes we pushed kernel update last week. average throughput improved ~6% but we started to see the 99th jump for TTFT in about 0.8% of requests. that's the microburst we want to address.
[01:22] Sasha: the weird part is the spikes don't align to payload size alone — we saw short prompts also hit the spike.
[01:29] Priya: could be because of prefix/persistent kv cache mis-hit — if the KV cache isn't warm or probe hits a cold shard that triggers a path that costs extra setup.
[01:42] Tanya: our SRE saw correlation with certain client regions — east-us2 more often. could be network handshake variance interacting with streaming socket warmup.
[01:53] Priya: good point. streaming handshake latency + kernel switch creates a coupling. polyphase hedging might help — start with a narrow, fast kernel for first token and if the request continues, switch to the wider kernel for throughput. it's a tradeoff but lowers median TTFT.
[02:10] Jordan: can you sketch how polyphase would work in our runtime?
[02:15] Priya: sure — phase one: ultra-low-latency kernel, optimized for sequence scaffolding and minimal kv ops; phase two: after token 8 or after 80ms, switch to the high-throughput kernel and restore full kv semantics. switching costs are small vs the TTFT benefit. we can hedge by replicating first token generation on both kernels for a few ms.
[02:34] Miguel: replicating sounds expensive for CPU or GPU. how much extra cost are we talking?
[02:39] Priya: marginal — for short outputs it's negligible. we estimate a 3-5% GPU utilization bump in worst case; we can gate it by percent of requests or seqlen distribution.
[02:50] Sasha: is there a ready config we can toggle? we don't want to recompile.
[02:55] Priya: we can ship a runtime flag — no recompilation. priority is to test in a canary pool. i can prepare config diffs.
[03:04] Luca: quick process note — we've got a security checklist for on-prem; robert, we may need your SSO team to confirm SAML attributes if we spin up customer-private nodes.
[03:14] Robert: yep we'll sync with SSO.
[03:17] [03:20] Sasha: i want to call out seqlen skew: our traffic is bimodal — chatty small prompts and a small fraction of long context docs (5-10%) up to 6k tokens. that long tail is what looks to flip kernel selection.
[03:33] Priya: perfect detail — that's why we recommended seqlen-aware routing: route long contexts to a pool tuned for high seqlen, and route short interactive to the fast path.
[03:42] Miguel: can routing be runtime policy? or do we need a pre-ingest classifier?
[03:47] Priya: runtime policy is fine: inspect request.seqlen header or token count in the gateway and tag. pre-ingest classifier only needed for ambiguous cases.
[03:55] Tanya: and how about streaming vs non-streaming? some calls are chunked so gateways see chunked content and delay seqlen calc.
[04:03] Priya: right — we estimate handshake reduction by deferring kernel heavy ops until after first chunk but also priming the narrow kernel at handshake. small engineering change.
[04:14] Sasha: any bench numbers?
[04:17] Priya: quick numbers from our lab: with polyphase hedging median TTFT down by ~120ms, 95th down by ~220ms, 99th down by ~430ms on our sample mixed workload. but worst-case GPU cost up 3-5%. i'll attach the raw perf sheet.
[04:34] Jordan: that sounds promising. are there other knobs — quant, batching, caching?
[04:38] Priya: yes — quantization profile shift helped but introduced small quality delta on some prompts. caching: prefix/KV cache warmup policy changes reduce miss cascade; batching: lower max-batch for low-latency pool, allow large batch in high-seqlen pool.
[04:52] Miguel: for our compliance team we need to understand the fallback behavior - if the fast kernel fails, do requests fall back to hosted or dedicated?
[04:59] Jordan: fallback policy currently can route to dedicated pool or broaden to a general pool in same region. we can set an automatic fallback to the high-seq pool.
[05:08] Sasha: we want to keep data in our VPC for the pilot — can polyphase run in Private deployment?
[05:13] Priya: absolutely; polyphase is runtime-level, so it's in the deployable runtime. for Private we'd push the same runtime and config diffs. security checks are the same.
[05:22] Tanya: on access, we'll need a small change to IP allow list and a jumpbox. i'll add that as an action item.
[05:28] [05:30] Robert: any blockers from Redwood side for an A/B kernel test?
[05:34] Priya: not blocker — we need the anonymized logs and a 2-hour slot to run kernel A vs kernel B with your traffic samples. we should run it on a canary pool with seqlen routing enabled.
[05:46] Sasha: i'll assemble logs — note they contain PII in some cases, we'll scrub before sending.
[05:51] Jordan: perfect. timeline — priya will share the perf spreadsheet and exact config diffs by friday (2027-11-19), a Doodle for the 2-hr lab goes out by thurs (2027-11-18). aurelia to send logs and 500 sample prompts by friday.
[06:05] Miguel: small ask — can we get a synthetic loader that reproduces the bimodal seqlen distribution so our infra folks can simulate?
[06:12] Priya: yes, we have a loader script. i'll package it and include sample config for your perf lab.
[06:18] Luca: i'll attach the security checklist and onboarding doc to the notes.
[06:22] Sasha: great. last question — competitors, we've run comparison vs anthro... anthropic earlier this year, they had lower 99th but cost higher. any notes?
[06:32] Jordan: noted — we'll include a short competitive note, but focus first on triage.
[06:36] Priya: closing — i'll push a small runtime flag PR for streaming handshake reduction (no recompile) to our canary; aim to have numbers by mon-wed.
[06:45] Jordan: thanks everyone, next sync after the A/B lab or earlier if blockers.
[06:50] End of recording
